list_child.name: list_licenses
list_child.desc: Returns the full set of content licensing deals currently tracked in the catalog system, spanning every stage from negotiation through expiration. This call is intended for building a complete picture of the licensing pipeline rather than checking a single deal.

get_child.name: get_license
get_child.desc: Retrieves the full record for a single licensing deal by its identifier, including its current stage and key dates. Use this when a specific deal needs a closer look rather than the entire catalog.

list_parent.name: list_studios
list_parent.desc: Returns every studio the platform has an existing or historical relationship with, independent of whether they currently have a live deal. This is useful for surveying the full roster of content partners.

get_parent.name: get_studio
get_parent.desc: Retrieves a single studio's record by id, including the name on file for that partner. It does not include the list of deals associated with that studio.

delete_child.name: terminate_license
delete_child.desc: Permanently terminates a licensing deal and removes it from the active catalog pipeline. This action cannot be reversed, so it should only be used once the termination is confirmed with legal.

set_enum.name: set_license_stage
set_enum.desc: Advances or reverts a licensing deal's stage among negotiating, signed, live, and expired. Content operations relies on this field to know exactly where a title stands in the acquisition pipeline.

set_bool.name: flag_exclusive
set_bool.desc: Marks a licensing deal as exclusive to the platform, meaning the title cannot appear on a competing service during the term. Marketing depends on this flag when planning launch campaigns.

set_ref.name: reassign_studio
set_ref.desc: Transfers a licensing deal from one studio's account to another, updating the counterparty of record. This is typically used when rights change hands between studios mid-negotiation.

send.name: message_studio
send.desc: Sends a message to the studio associated with a given licensing deal, or to a named studio directly. This is the standard channel content operations uses to relay contractual updates.
